items.question: What worldly honor accrues to those devoted practitioners?
premises: They become possessors of fame.
They receive honor from kings.
items.inference: Devoted practitioners attain renown and royal respect.
items.plain_english: They may become famous and honored by kings.

items.question: What protection from external dangers do such practitioners gain?
premises: Boats and similar sources pose danger.
Fear from these does not arise for them.
items.inference: Practitioners are freed from fear of external perils.
items.plain_english: They would have no fear even from boats and such dangers.

items.question: Why would others willingly enter service to such a practitioner?
premises: Others approach him with devotion.
Devotion leads them to accept servitude.
items.inference: His power naturally draws others into devoted service.
items.plain_english: How could they not, out of devotion, come to serve him?

items.question: What exclusive devotion do excellent women show toward him?
premises: Excellent women attend upon him.
They do not pursue other arts or attachments.
items.inference: He commands the exclusive devotion of excellent women.
items.plain_english: Excellent women, devoted to no other arts, attend upon him.

items.question: How does a hostile warrior fare when confronting him directly?
premises: A hostile warrior may come face to face.
Such confrontation is presented as ineffective.
items.inference: Even direct opposition by a warrior is overcome.
uncertainties: The consequence is completed in the following verse.
items.plain_english: Even when another warrior comes face to face with him...

items.question: What loss of strength befalls opponents facing the practitioner?
premises: Opponents confront the practitioner.
Their vigor becomes struck down.
items.inference: Opponents are rendered powerless before him.
items.plain_english: How could his opponents not become stripped of their strength?

items.question: Why might former enemies seek refuge with this practitioner?
premises: Enemies recognize his power.
Seeking refuge becomes their response.
items.inference: Even enemies are compelled to take refuge in him.
items.plain_english: How could his enemies not come to him for refuge?

items.question: Can thieves or bandits inflict harm upon the practitioner?
premises: Thieves are potential sources of harm.
They are unable to cause obstruction.
items.inference: The practitioner is protected even from thieves.
items.plain_english: Even thieves would not be able to cause him any harm.

items.question: Do hostile spirits ever intrude upon the practitioner's domain?
premises: Spirits might be expected to intrude.
They never enter there.
items.inference: The practitioner's domain is inaccessible to hostile spirits.
items.plain_english: Nor do spirits ever enter there.

items.question: Can any obstacle be created against the practitioner under any circumstances?
premises: Obstacles might arise in various ways.
None can be created against him.
items.inference: The practitioner remains free from all obstacles.
items.plain_english: They could not create any obstacle for him in any way at all.

rows.grounds: this newly revealed lord or text

items.question: What purpose does this newly revealed lordly teaching serve?
premises: Immaturity requires removal.
This new lordly teaching is directed to that removal.
items.inference: The teaching is intended to remove spiritual immaturity.
uncertainties: nava+īśam+enam may refer to a text or a form of the lord.
items.plain_english: This new lordly teaching is for the removal of immaturity.

rows.grounds: the supreme goal to be attained

items.question: What ultimate attainment does this teaching lead to over time?
premises: The path unfolds over a long time.
It culminates in the infinite supreme goal.
items.inference: The teaching ultimately leads to the infinite supreme attainment.
items.plain_english: In the end, after a long time, it leads to the infinite, supreme attainment.

rows.grounds: one should recite it always even with an uncollected mind

items.question: What benefit comes from reciting this teaching even without mental composure?
premises: The teaching is conducive to heaven.
It should be recited always, even with an uncollected mind.
items.inference: Constant recitation yields benefit despite lack of mental composure.
items.plain_english: One should always recite this heaven-leading teaching, even with an uncollected mind.

rows.grounds: or one who desires to hear all things

items.question: Who is encouraged to listen attentively to this teaching?
premises: Listening to the teaching is enjoined.
One who wishes to hear all should listen.
items.inference: The teaching invites attentive hearing from those eager to learn.
items.plain_english: One should listen to it, or anyone who wishes to hear everything should do so.

rows.grounds: rhetorical: whom would it not delight
the sole cause of true personhood

items.question: Why does this teaching delight all as the sole cause of true personhood?
premises: The teaching is the sole cause of true personhood.
Such a cause naturally brings delight.
items.inference: As the sole ground of true personhood, it delights everyone.
items.plain_english: Whom here would it not delight, being the sole cause of true personhood?

rows.grounds: this teaching that has been declared

items.question: How does this all-encompassing teaching function to destroy sin?
premises: This declared teaching is all-encompassing in form.
It serves to destroy sin.
items.inference: The all-formed teaching declared here destroys sin completely.
items.plain_english: This declared teaching, all-encompassing in every way, serves to destroy sin.

rows.grounds: those who worship the primordial power

items.question: What path of ascent opens for those who worship the primordial power?
premises: Some worship the primordial power.
They are urged to ascend the path of great bliss.
items.inference: Worship of the primordial power leads to ascent on the blissful path.
items.plain_english: Ascend, ascend the path of great bliss, you who worship the primordial power.

rows.grounds: remover of fear born from worldly existence

items.question: What divine qualities define the goddess addressed in this invocation?
premises: She is of the nature of Śiva and companion to Śiva.
She removes fear born of worldly existence.
items.inference: The invoked goddess embodies Śiva-nature and removes existential fear.
items.plain_english: O you who consist of Śiva, friend of Śiva, remover of the fear born of existence!

items.question: What boons and nature does the goddess offer to her devotees?
premises: She is the giver of the supreme boon to devotees.
Her form is complete auspiciousness.
items.inference: The goddess grants the highest boon and embodies full auspiciousness for devotees.
items.plain_english: She is the giver of the supreme boon to devotees, whose form is complete auspiciousness.

items.question: How is the goddess Lalitā identified within this named poetic work?
premises: The work is named the sport of names.
Lalitā appears as the sixteenfold goddess of full fame.
items.inference: In this work, Lalitā is celebrated as the renowned sixteenfold goddess.
items.plain_english: In this poem named the Sport of Names, Lalitā is the sixteenfold goddess of full renown.

rows.grounds: the Kaula way or knower; see ledger

items.question: What complete state of the great goddess is associated with the Kaula way?
premises: The Kaula way is invoked.
It relates to the complete state of the great goddess.
items.inference: The Kaula way embodies the complete fullness of the great goddess.
uncertainties: Syntactic role may continue from or into adjacent verses.
items.plain_english: The Kaula way is the complete state of the great goddess.

items.question: How is devotion identified in relation to the sixteenfold goddess?
premises: The sixteenfold goddess is named.
Devotion is equated or closely linked with her.
items.inference: Devotion is identified with the sixteenfold goddess.
uncertainties: The predication may depend on surrounding verses.
items.plain_english: The sixteenfold goddess is devotion.

items.question: What metaphor describes the agents that accomplish purification in this context?
premises: Purification of that state is being accomplished.
Certain agents are likened to extractors of nectar.
items.inference: The agents of purification are metaphorically described as nectar-extractors.
uncertainties: The compound cakoraka+taka+kṣodāḥ is obscure and metaphorical.
items.plain_english: In accomplishing its purification, they are like fine particles that extract nectar.

rows.grounds: statement of knowledge or its limit
when all is equal or same

items.question: In what equal state can the superiority of a truly good person be discerned?
premises: The speaker claims not to know the answer.
The superiority of a good person is questioned in an equal state.
items.inference: The superiority of a truly good person transcends ordinary equal conditions.
items.plain_english: We do not know in what equal state the superiority of a truly good person could be found.
